We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide bond to give acid and aniline (or amine). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aromatic ring (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: amide between carbonyl (attached to alkene) and aniline (aniline with NH2). So precursor 1: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (with phenyl attached to alkene) i.e., /C=C/C(=O) (attached to phenyl). Actually target has /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Wait: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So carbonyl attached to N which attached to phenyl with NH2 (aniline). So amide formation step: carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated) + 4-aminophenyl? Actually the amine is an aniline with NH2 (para? not important). So step 1: break amide to give unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Good.

Step 2: The unsaturated acid derived from Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (likely 4-formyl phenyl attached to sulfonyl phenyl?) Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl sulfonyl group via aromatic ring: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)...)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So the aldehyde would be the aromatic aldehyde with sulfonyl phenyl attached? The Doebner modification forms the α,β-unsaturated acid attached to the aromatic ring where aldehyde is attached. So we need aldehyde: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group? The aldehyde is on the same phenyl that later gets sulfonylated? Actually sulfonamide formation is between an amine (the first phenyl ring with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl chloride (maybe from sulfonyl chloride reacting with amine). The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl ring (c2ccc...). So the sulfonamide formation step: amine (first phenyl with methyl) + sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) -> sulfonamide linking the two phenyls. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride). The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl ring which also bears the unsaturated acid side chain. So precursor: aryl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2) with side chain unsaturated acid attached at para position? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring via S=O2Cl attached to the phenyl (Ar-SO2Cl). In target, the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(...). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be Cl-S(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(...). So step 3: sulfonamide formation.

Thus overall retrosynthesis:

Target -> (1) amide disconnection -> unsaturated acid (A) + aniline (B)

A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1? Wait unsaturated acid still attached to sulfonyl phenyl. So A is the same as target but with COOH instead of CONH-Ph-NH2? Actually the amide is on the side chain attached to second phenyl: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So after breaking amide, we have unsaturated acid attached to second phenyl: /C=C/COOH (still attached to phenyl). So A = Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1.

B = aniline (c3ccccc3N) (para? not needed). So step 1 template: amide formation (reverse). Need template ID for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine). We haven't found yet. Could search for functional_groups_broken: ["aliphatic carboxylic acid"] and formed: ["amide"] but earlier error due to using "carboxylic acid" not "aliphatic carboxylic acid". Let's try again with correct group.
